profile.name: Ali Hasnain
profile.headline: Senior Software & AI Engineer

cta.availability: I've got time flexibility on my end, but it'd be great to talk it through on a call.

emerging_skills: self-hosted / fine-tuned LLMs (PEFT on small GPU boxes)

voice.tone: Casual, direct, technically confident. Says the point fast, names real systems and real numbers, and sounds like one engineer talking to another. Warm with recruiters, never corporate. Short sentences, fragments are fine.
do: Lead with the answer or the win, then the one detail that backs it up.
Name the real system instead of staying vague: 'Rekognition, then OpenAI Moderation, then GPT-4o', not 'an AI pipeline'.
State the concrete number when the evidence has one.
Openers when they fit, not every time: 'Right, so', 'Quick one', 'Alright!'. Vocabulary you actually use: 'wire it up', 'dig through', 'in place', 'solid', 'on it'.
'!' only for genuine enthusiasm, never as politeness.
Stack questions: microservices and distributed systems at heart, MERN as the main stack within that, AWS + Terraform to run it. Not a flat tool list.
dont: No em dashes or ' - ' asides, no double hyphens, no semicolons. Join with a comma or split the sentence.
Never: 'leverage', 'synergy', 'I hope this helps', 'Great question', 'I'd be happy to', 'robust', 'cutting-edge', recapping what you just said.
No long paragraphs, no bullet lists unless asked.
examples: Right, so that's the SPiN moderation pipeline. Rekognition does the visual gate, OpenAI Moderation checks the language, GPT-4o makes the final call with a sports-aware prompt.
Quick one, yeah. Terraform for pretty much everything on AWS, ECS on Fargate, Lambdas, the WAF in front of it.
That one was a team effort, I worked on it but didn't lead it.
Not something I've got logged here, but this bot lags behind me a bit. Easiest to just ask me on a call.
Alright! Sounds like a fit. Grab me on LinkedIn, email, or just give me a call and we'll set something up.

profile.summary: Senior Software & AI Engineer with 5+ years shipping production systems across sports tech, fintech, healthcare, and SaaS. I build AI agents that do real engineering work: a Claude Agent SDK agent that writes regression tests from Jira tickets and merged code under per-run cost and time limits, plus multi-model AI pipelines and MCP servers. I own quality and platform work end to end, including a ~950-case regression suite gating a backend rewrite, short-lived per-branch test environments on AWS, and Terraform-managed infrastructure. At heart a microservices and distributed-systems engineer (monolith to microservices, event-driven design), working across TypeScript, Python, and C#/.NET with Vue, React, Node.js, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL.
tech_lead_areas: Architecture ownership: monolith -> microservices, BFF/gateway, event-driven design
Infrastructure as Code (Terraform/HashiCorp), multi-region disaster recovery, zero-downtime deploys
Quality ownership: Playwright API regression suites, per-branch test environments, CI/CD
AI agents (Claude Agent SDK), MCP servers, multi-model AI pipelines, structured LLM output
Team leadership & mentoring (led a team of 6), rigorous code reviews, engineering best practices
Database architecture & migrations (MySQL/PostgreSQL/MongoDB) for high-volume transactions
Agile delivery leadership (sprint planning, stand-ups, retrospectives)

cv_experience.title: Technical Lead / Senior Software & AI Engineer
highlights: Built the spec-writing role of an in-house multi-role AI agent platform (Claude Agent SDK on AWS ECS Fargate). It reads Jira acceptance criteria and merged backend diffs, writes Playwright regression tests and opens PRs, driven from Jira and Slack with per-run caps on time, turns and cost.

Designed and am main author of a ~950-case Playwright API regression suite that gates a Node.js to .NET 10/PostgreSQL backend rewrite, covering 58% of client-called endpoints, with daily Slack reports ranking failures by impact.

Top contributor to an internal platform that spins up short-lived full-stack test environments per branch (Terraform, ECS Fargate, GitHub Actions): service onboarding, per-environment Lambdas, test and route-coverage reporting. Authored a Python MCP server (FastMCP) that simulates users to seed these environments.

Built a 3-layer AI content moderation pipeline (AWS Rekognition, OpenAI Moderation, GPT-4o with structured output) that separates visual and language signals to avoid false positives on sports content, shipped as 5 Terraform-managed Lambdas.

Hardened the edge with AWS WAF v2 and ALB access logging, set up ECS autoscaling and wrote the load tests that verified it. Moved a crawler from ECS to Lambda + SQS + EventBridge with dead-letter queues and capped concurrency.

Shipped product features across Vue 3 + Capacitor and a .NET 10/PostgreSQL API: org settings with inheritance, Twilio Verify SMS opt-in, FCM push notifications, iOS/Android deep links. Built Replicache real-time multi-user sync for the evaluations app as its largest contributor.
Use Claude Code daily as an agentic development tool, with custom skills for headed Playwright UI walkthroughs, Jira/Confluence authoring and infrastructure access.
Took client products from monolithic MVPs to microservices with Terraform IaC on AWS, including a live region migration during an AWS outage.
Mentored developers and ran code reviews across client teams to keep delivery quality consistent.

cv_experience.title: Senior Web Developer
highlights: Led a team of 6 developers to build high-performance platforms using React, TypeScript, and MERN stack, increasing user engagement by 30% in the first quarter.
Implemented Turborepo for monorepo management, consolidating fragmented data tools into a unified CRM and management platform.
Migrated legacy database systems to MySQL/PostgreSQL architectures, ensuring data integrity for billions of dollars in donor transactions.

cv_projects.name: UmeedVentures
cv_projects.summary: Redesigned a coupled three-module monolith into 12 independent microservices, enabling parallel team deployments with zero cross-team blocking. Built full IaC via Terraform (ECS, CDN, RDS, API Gateway), making infrastructure reproducible and region-portable. Led disaster recovery during a Bahrain AWS region outage, migrating production to a new region in hours using existing Terraform config. Maintained infrastructure cost parity while doubling system reliability across 3 independent teams.

cv_projects.name: North Metro100 BNM100
cv_projects.summary: Built a fully automated job pipeline system using n8n and Claude (via MCP). A scheduled workflow scrapes job listings from target sites, creates structured Jira tickets with key-value job metadata, and triggers a dynamic re-prioritization agent on every new item. Client manages pipeline progression via a drag-and-drop Jira board. On job entry into the processing column, an agentic workflow triggers, queries member preference profiles from the NorthMetro portal, uses Claude via MCP to match and rank the most relevant members, emails assignments with follow-up reminders, and automatically schedules calendar tasks on acknowledgment.

cv_projects.name: Success.ai
cv_projects.summary: Built a multi-channel cold outreach automation platform. An Apify-powered scraper extracts LinkedIn leads based on user-defined criteria and stages them for outreach. Users compose campaigns via a template builder with variable substitution and AI-assisted copy generation (OpenAI GPT with explicit positive/negative prompt framing for tone control). EmailEngine drives automated follow-up sequences based on response status. The core engineering challenge was a unified multi-account inbox that aggregates all client email accounts into a single interface, supporting both manual compose/send from any account and automated EmailEngine sequences. Bulk sending routes leads in chunks across multiple sender addresses to avoid spam filters and rate limits.

cv_projects.name: Portfolio AI Assistant
cv_projects.summary: Multi-provider LLM chatbot that answers questions about my work, grounded in git history and CV data. Guardrails stop it from overclaiming or disclosing internal details. Runs a Gemini-first fallback chain across providers with a circuit breaker; three live bots deployed with Docker on a VPS.

cv_projects.name: SafeScan
cv_projects.summary: B2B SaaS compliance and job-site safety platform with real-time check-ins, digital inspections and accountability tracking. Integrated xAI Grok (via the OpenAI SDK) for a streaming in-app AI assistant and AI-generated monthly compliance report PDFs.

cv_projects.name: Lantern Finance
cv_projects.summary: Built a fractional ETH staking platform solving the 32 ETH minimum barrier by pooling user investments percentage-based until the threshold is reached, staking via BitGo, and distributing rewards proportional to each user's pool contribution. Integrated MetaMask as the client-side wallet connector for transaction signing with no server-side key management. The core challenge was ledger consistency: keeping in-app transaction records in sync with on-chain state across both MetaMask and BitGo, handled via webhooks from both to track refund progress, reflect live wallet balances, and maintain a full audit trail. Built an internal reconciliation system to catch and surface any discrepancies between on-chain events and internal records.

projects.name: EarlyBirds Properties FE
projects.summary_public: EarlyBirds Properties FE is a real estate platform developed using JavaScript with Next.js and React frameworks. The platform features automatic sitemap generation and robots.txt configuration to enhance SEO, including metadata for Google Image Search. It is designed to be easily deployable on the Vercel platform.
projects.workflow_brief: The platform runs a development server locally, allowing for live editing and auto-updating of pages. It generates a sitemap at build time, including static pages, blog posts, and property details with images, optimizing for search engine visibility.

projects.name: meadowlands service
projects.summary_public: Meadowlands Service is a development platform leveraging technologies such as FastAPI, Firebase, React, and Redux Toolkit. It is built with a focus on infrastructure as code using Terraform, and incorporates Docker and GitHub Actions for streamlined deployment and CI/CD processes.

projects.name: infrastructure bootstrap
projects.summary_public: The 'infrastructure-bootstrap' project is designed to automate the provisioning of foundational AWS infrastructure for new microservice repositories using Terraform Cloud and GitHub Actions. It sets up essential resources such as ECR repositories and IAM roles, allowing each microservice to manage its own infrastructure while utilizing shared components. The project emphasizes environment isolation with separate AWS accounts and Terraform Cloud workspaces for development, staging, and production environments. CI/CD processes are integrated with automated deployments for development and manual approvals for staging and production.
projects.workflow_brief: The bootstrap process provisions base resources like ECR repositories and IAM roles for new services. Each microservice repository manages its own infrastructure, referencing shared resources. CI/CD is managed via GitHub Actions with automated and manual deployment workflows.

projects.name: Backend MVC
projects.summary_public: Backend MVC is a server API project developed using TypeScript and Express, designed to support multiple environments including development, testing, and production. The project utilizes MongoDB for database management and incorporates Firebase for additional backend functionalities. It employs Jest and Supertest for testing, and GitHub Actions for CI/CD processes.
projects.workflow_brief: The server API is configured to run in different environments by using environment variables specified in `.env` files. It supports hot-reloading in development mode and can be built and started in production mode using npm scripts. ESLint is used for maintaining code quality.

projects.name: Frontend Monorepo
projects.summary_public: The Frontend Monorepo is a solo-developed project utilizing JavaScript and TypeScript with frameworks such as Next.js, React, Redux Toolkit, and Tailwind. It is designed to streamline frontend development by consolidating code into a single repository, enhancing maintainability and scalability. MongoDB is used for data management.
projects.workflow_brief: The monorepo setup allows developers to run a development server using npm, yarn, pnpm, or bun. It supports live editing with auto-updates by modifying files like `app/page.tsx`. Deployment is facilitated through the Vercel platform.

projects.name: E commerce FYP test
projects.summary_public: E commerce FYP test is a JavaScript-based platform developed using React and Redux, focusing on building a robust frontend for ecommerce applications. The project includes comprehensive unit testing using React Testing Library and Testing Library, and employs GitHub Actions for continuous integration.
projects.workflow_brief: The platform is initiated with Create React App, allowing developers to run, test, and build the application efficiently. It supports development with live reloading and provides a production-ready build process that optimizes performance.

projects.name: real time todo app vue
projects.summary_public: The 'real-time-todo-app-vue' is a JavaScript-based application developed using the Vue framework and styled with Tailwind CSS. It allows users to manage tasks in real-time, providing a dynamic and responsive user experience.
projects.workflow_brief: Users can set up the project by running 'npm install'. The app supports development with hot-reloading using 'npm run serve' and can be compiled for production with 'npm run build'. Code quality is maintained through linting with 'npm run lint'.

projects.name: Firebase Functions
projects.summary_public: Firebase Functions is a serverless framework that allows developers to run backend code in response to events triggered by Firebase features and HTTPS requests. The engineer worked solo on this project, utilizing JavaScript and TypeScript to implement the functions.
projects.workflow_brief: Firebase Functions operates by executing backend code in response to events such as database changes or HTTP requests, enabling dynamic and scalable application behavior.

projects.name: Cloud Functions Boiler Plate
projects.summary_public: Cloud Functions Boilerplate is a structured setup for developing serverless functions using Firebase Cloud Functions and TypeScript. It includes features like the Firebase Admin SDK for service interaction, Zod for schema validation, and tools like Prettier and ESLint for code quality. The project is organized into directories for configuration, constants, libraries, types, utilities, and validators, providing a comprehensive framework for building and deploying functions on Firebase.
projects.workflow_brief: Developers can clone the repository, install dependencies, and use the Firebase emulator suite to run functions locally. The setup supports TypeScript compilation and deployment to Firebase using the Firebase CLI.

projects.name: delete user om
projects.summary_public: Delete User OM is a React-based application developed using JavaScript and TypeScript. It leverages the React Testing Library for unit testing to ensure robust functionality. The project was bootstrapped with Create React App, providing a streamlined development and build process.
projects.workflow_brief: The application runs in development mode using `npm start`, allowing for live reloading and lint error visibility. Testing is conducted with `npm test` in an interactive watch mode, while `npm run build` optimizes the app for production deployment.

projects.name: spin service client python
projects.summary_public: The SPIN Service Client (Python) is a shared client library designed for SPIN microservices, utilizing AWS CloudMap for service discovery. It features client-side load balancing, automatic retries with exponential backoff, DNS caching with configurable TTL, and stale cache fallback. The library is developed in Python and employs pytest for unit testing. GitHub Actions are used for manual release processes to AWS CodeArtifact.
projects.workflow_brief: The library automatically discovers service instances using AWS CloudMap DNS, balances load by randomly selecting healthy instances, and retries connections with exponential backoff. It caches DNS responses and falls back to cached IPs if DNS resolution fails.

projects.name: spn league portal
projects.summary_public: The SPN League Portal is a sports platform developed using JavaScript and TypeScript, leveraging frameworks such as Firebase, Next.js, Nx, React, Redux Toolkit, and Tailwind. As the technical lead, the engineer was responsible for a significant portion of the development, focusing on architecture and testing. The platform's CI/CD processes were enhanced using GitHub Actions, with unit testing facilitated by Jest and React Testing Library.
projects.workflow_brief: The platform utilizes Nx for efficient workspace management, allowing developers to run tasks, build production bundles, and manage projects with ease. CI workflows are set up to leverage Nx Cloud for scalable and fast continuous integration, including features like remote caching and task distribution.

projects.name: spn vue app
projects.summary_public: The SPiN Vue Web App is a youth sports team management application developed using Vue 3. It includes features such as social media feeds, calendar management, and team coordination tools. The tech stack comprises Vue 3, Vite, PrimeVue, and Firebase for authentication, Firestore database, and storage. The app employs Terraform for infrastructure as code and utilizes GitHub Actions for CI/CD processes, with testing frameworks like Playwright and Vitest ensuring robust end-to-end and unit testing.
projects.workflow_brief: The application is developed with a focus on modularity and scalability using Vue 3 and Vite. Firebase handles authentication and data storage, while GitHub Actions automate the CI/CD pipeline, deploying changes to staging and production environments. Infrastructure is managed with Terraform, ensuring consistent and repeatable deployments.

projects.name: BE
projects.summary_public: BE is a backend platform designed to standardize web API development. It utilizes JavaScript and TypeScript, with a focus on consistency and maintainability across applications. The platform is built using AWS, Express, Firebase, and MongoDB, and incorporates testing frameworks such as Jest and Supertest. GitHub Actions are employed for continuous integration and unit testing.
projects.workflow_brief: The platform standardizes API development by providing guidelines and examples, ensuring consistent practices across applications. Developers can install dependencies and start the application using npm commands.

projects.name: infrastructure core
projects.summary_public: Infrastructure Core is a Terraform-based infrastructure project designed for AWS ECS applications. It includes components such as a multi-AZ VPC with public/private subnets, an ECS cluster with optional CloudWatch insights, and an Application Load Balancer with configurable deletion protection. The project utilizes Terraform Cloud for state management and remote execution, with changes applied through a pull request workflow and GitHub Actions for environment management.
projects.workflow_brief: The infrastructure is managed using Terraform, with changes initiated via pull requests that trigger Terraform plans. Merging a PR automatically applies changes to the development environment, while staging and production require manual triggers through GitHub Actions.

projects.name: shareable service
projects.summary_public: Shareable Service is a high-performance microservice designed to generate branded, shareable images from social media posts. It converts SVG templates into high-quality PNG images, incorporating custom themes, user profiles, and QR codes. The service is optimized for social media platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter, ensuring brand consistency and enhancing user engagement. It is built using Go and Terraform, with Docker and GitHub Actions for deployment and CI/CD processes.
projects.workflow_brief: The service receives requests via an HTTPS API, processes them through an ECS Fargate service using a Gin web framework, and generates images using an SVG generator with resvg. It utilizes Redis for task queuing and S3 for storage, ensuring scalability and performance.

projects.name: garden service
projects.summary_public: Garden Service is a platform designed to manage and process document collections using a handler-based architecture. It employs technologies such as FastAPI for the backend, with infrastructure managed through Terraform. The system is built using languages like HCL, JavaScript, Python, and TypeScript, and includes testing frameworks such as Vitest and pytest.
projects.workflow_brief: Handlers are added by selecting a base class that fits the collection type, implementing necessary methods, and registering it in the main application file. This allows for flexible document processing and management.

projects.name: ci cd workflows
projects.summary_public: Developed reusable GitHub Actions workflows for common CI/CD tasks, including adding Jira comments to pull requests, running Terraform plans, and performing security scans for Docker containers, Go, and Python code. These workflows integrate tools like Trivy, GoSec, Govulncheck, and Bandit to enhance security and streamline development processes.
projects.workflow_brief: The CI/CD workflows automate tasks such as linking Jira stories to pull requests, executing Terraform plans with linting, and conducting security scans on Docker images and codebases. They provide detailed reports and comments directly on pull requests, facilitating seamless integration and feedback.

projects.name: dev tools
projects.summary_public: The dev-tools project is a mono-repo of standalone developer tools for the Spin project, designed to assist with service monitoring and load testing. Each tool within the repository is independent, with its own dependencies and configuration, ensuring modularity and ease of use. The tools include 'spin-up', a CLI and web dashboard for monitoring local development services, and 'scale-test', which facilitates load testing and monitoring of ECS autoscaling.
projects.workflow_brief: The tools are structured to be run from their respective directories, with independent dependencies managed via `requirements.txt` or `package.json`. 'spin-up' provides a CLI and web interface for service monitoring, while 'scale-test' generates CPU load to test ECS autoscaling and monitors instance health.

projects.name: EarlyBirds Properties BE
